name: AWS data plane access logs
description: Request- and flow-level access logs from four AWS data-plane services (Application Load Balancer, S3, CloudFront, Transit Gateway), as the Splunk Add-on for AWS ingests each from S3 delivery.
source: AWS's own log-format reference pages for each service, checked against a live dev Splunk instance seeded with Splunk_TA_aws and, where available, AWS's own worked sample log lines.

feed.label: AWS data plane access logs
feed.description: What was requested, by whom, from where, with what result, across a load balancer, a bucket, an edge network and a transit gateway.

access_client_ip.label: Client address
access_client_ip.description: The IP address of the requester as the AWS edge or load balancer saw it: a proxy's or load balancer's address in front of the real client, not necessarily the real client.

access_dest_ip.label: Destination address
access_dest_ip.description: The IP address the traffic was addressed to on the far side of the flow.

access_client_port.label: Client port
access_client_port.description: The TCP or UDP port the requester connected from.

access_dest_port.label: Destination port
access_dest_port.description: The TCP or UDP port on the target or destination side of the connection.

access_http_status.label: HTTP status
access_http_status.description: The numeric HTTP status code of the response, as this tier generated or observed it.

access_user_agent.label: User agent
access_user_agent.description: The client's User-Agent header, quoted as sent.

access_http_method.label: HTTP method
access_http_method.description: The HTTP request method (GET, PUT, POST, and so on).

access_domain.label: Host
access_domain.description: The domain the request was addressed to: an SNI value, a Host header, or the endpoint the client connected to, depending on the sourcetype.

access_request_id.label: Request id
access_request_id.description: An id that ties one request (or, for ELB, one X-Ray trace) to this one log record.

access_bytes_out.label: Response bytes
access_bytes_out.description: The size in bytes of the response sent to the client.

access_bytes_in.label: Request bytes
access_bytes_in.description: The size in bytes of the request received from the client.

elb_type.label: Listener type
elb_type.description: The type of request or connection the listener handled.

elb_response_time.label: Response time
elb_response_time.description: When the load balancer generated a response to the client (ISO 8601); for WebSockets, when the connection closed. This sourcetype's time field.

elb_request_creation_time.label: Request creation time
elb_request_creation_time.description: When the load balancer received the request from the client (ISO 8601).

elb_id.label: Load balancer id
elb_id.description: The resource id of the load balancer; can contain forward slashes.

elb_target_status_code.label: Target status code
elb_target_status_code.description: The HTTP status code of the response from the target itself, recorded only when a connection to the target was established and it responded; a dash otherwise.

elb_request_line.label: Request line
elb_request_line.description: The client's request line, quoted: HTTP method, protocol://host:port/uri, HTTP version, exactly as the load balancer received it.

elb_target_group_arn.label: Target group ARN
elb_target_group_arn.description: The ARN of the target group the request was routed to.

elb_target_endpoint.label: Target endpoint
elb_target_endpoint.description: The IP address and port of the target that received the request, colon-joined exactly as this field arrives; a dash when no target received the request (for example a fixed response, a redirect, or a failed Lambda invocation). This TA does not split the field into separate IP and port columns.

elb_tls.label: TLS negotiation
elb_tls.description: The negotiated SSL/TLS cipher and protocol for an HTTPS listener; a dash on both bindings when the listener is not HTTPS.

elb_actions_executed.label: Actions taken
elb_actions_executed.description: The comma-separated list of actions the load balancer took while processing the request, quoted; a dash if none (for example a malformed request).

elb_error_reason.label: Error reason
elb_error_reason.description: The error reason code, quoted, when an authenticate or Lambda-target action failed; a dash otherwise.

elb_matched_rule_priority.label: Matched rule priority
elb_matched_rule_priority.description: The priority (1-50000) of the listener rule that matched, 0 if the default action was taken, -1 on a rules-evaluation error, or a dash for any other error.

s3_bucket_owner.label: Bucket owner / requester
s3_bucket_owner.description: The canonical user ID of the bucket owner or, on the requester binding, of whoever made the request (or the assumed-role ARN, or a dash if unauthenticated): another form of the AWS account ID, not the 12-digit account number itself.

s3_bucket_name.label: Bucket name
s3_bucket_name.description: The bucket the request was processed against.

s3_operation.label: Operation
s3_operation.description: The S3 operation, written as SOAP.op, REST.method.resource, WEBSITE.method.resource, BATCH.DELETE.OBJECT, or S3.action.resource; S3.COMPUTE.OBJECT.CHECKSUM for a Compute checksum job.

s3_key.label: Object key
s3_key.description: The key (object name) part of the request; a dash for an operation that takes no key, such as a bucket-level request.

s3_request_uri.label: Request-URI
s3_request_uri.description: The Request-URI part of the HTTP request message, quoted, including the query string.

s3_error_code.label: S3 error code
s3_error_code.description: The Amazon S3 error response code, or a dash when the request succeeded.

s3_object_size.label: Object size
s3_object_size.description: The total size in bytes of the object the request concerned; a dash when not applicable.

s3_total_time.label: Total time
s3_total_time.description: Milliseconds the request was in flight from S3's side: from receipt to the last response byte sent.

s3_turn_around_time.label: Turn-around time
s3_turn_around_time.description: Milliseconds S3 spent processing the request: from the last request byte received to the first response byte sent.

s3_request_time.label: Request time
s3_request_time.description: When the request was received, in UTC. This sourcetype's time field.

cf_edge_location.label: Edge location
cf_edge_location.description: The three-letter-plus-number code of the edge location that served the request (commonly the nearby airport's IATA code, for example NRT12-P4).

cf_edge_result.label: Edge cache result
cf_edge_result.description: How CloudFront classified the response against its cache: served from cache, revalidated, missed to origin, or one of the error, limit or redirect outcomes.

cf_protocol.label: Viewer protocol
cf_protocol.description: The protocol the viewer used for the request.

cf_protocol_version.label: HTTP version
cf_protocol_version.description: The HTTP version the viewer specified in the request.

cf_uri_stem.label: URI stem
cf_uri_stem.description: The path and object portion of the request URL; question marks and query strings are not included.

cf_uri_query.label: URI query
cf_uri_query.description: The query-string portion of the request URL; a dash when there is none.

cf_time_taken.label: Time taken
cf_time_taken.description: Seconds, to the thousandth, from receiving the viewer's request to writing the last response byte, as measured on the server.

cf_time_to_first_byte.label: Time to first byte
cf_time_to_first_byte.description: Seconds between receiving the request and writing the first response byte, as measured on the server.

cf_fle_status.label: Field-level encryption status
cf_fle_status.description: Whether a field-level-encryption-configured distribution processed the request body successfully; a dash when field-level encryption is not configured.

cf_tls.label: TLS negotiation
cf_tls.description: The negotiated SSL/TLS protocol and cipher when the request used HTTPS; a dash on both bindings when it used plain HTTP.

cf_event_time.label: Event time
cf_event_time.description: The UTC date and time CloudFront finished responding (or, for a WebSocket, when the connection closed); this sourcetype's time field is built from these two columns together.

cf_forwarded_client_ip.label: Forwarded client address
cf_forwarded_client_ip.description: The viewer's own IP address when it reached CloudFront through an HTTP proxy or load balancer, taken from the request's forwarding header; a dash when there was no proxy in the path.

cf_distribution_domain.label: Distribution domain
cf_distribution_domain.description: The CloudFront distribution's own domain name (its d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net form), regardless of what domain the viewer actually asked for.

tgw_id.label: Transit gateway id
tgw_id.description: The id of the transit gateway the flow was recorded on.

tgw_attachment_id.label: Attachment id
tgw_attachment_id.description: The id of the transit gateway attachment the flow was recorded on.

tgw_account_id.label: Owner account id
tgw_account_id.description: The AWS account id that owns the source transit gateway.

tgw_src_vpc_id.label: Source VPC id
tgw_src_vpc_id.description: The id of the source VPC for the transit gateway traffic.

tgw_dst_vpc_id.label: Destination VPC id
tgw_dst_vpc_id.description: The id of the destination VPC for the transit gateway traffic.

tgw_protocol.label: IANA protocol number
tgw_protocol.description: The IANA protocol number of the traffic (for example 6 for TCP, 17 for UDP).

tgw_packets.label: Packets
tgw_packets.description: The number of packets transferred during the flow's aggregation interval.

tgw_bytes.label: Bytes
tgw_bytes.description: The number of bytes transferred during the flow's aggregation interval.

tgw_flow_start.label: Flow start
tgw_flow_start.description: Unix seconds when the first packet of the flow was received within the aggregation interval; can be up to 60 seconds after the packet was actually seen.

tgw_flow_end.label: Flow end
tgw_flow_end.description: Unix seconds when the last packet of the flow was received within the aggregation interval; can be up to 60 seconds after the packet was actually seen.

tgw_log_status.label: Log status
tgw_log_status.description: Whether the flow log delivered normally, saw no traffic in the interval, or skipped records.

tgw_flow_direction.label: Flow direction
tgw_flow_direction.description: The direction of the flow relative to the transit gateway.

tgw_type.label: Traffic type
tgw_type.description: The IP or fabric type of the traffic in the flow.

aws:elb:accesslogs.description: Application Load Balancer access logs: one line per request (or, for WebSockets, per closed connection), delivered to S3 and pulled by the Splunk Add-on for AWS's generic S3 input. Space-delimited, with double-quoted fields for values that can contain spaces.
aws:elb:accesslogs.note: Sample: the awsdocs ALB user guide's three worked examples (HTTP, HTTPS, a failed Lambda target), frozen at field 25 (error_reason); the live page has since grown to 34 fields (target:port_list onward) that this snapshot does not carry. Source: AWS Elastic Load Balancing User Guide for Application Load Balancers, 'Access log entry examples', https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-access-logs.html.

aws:s3:accesslogs.description: Amazon S3 server access logs: one line per request against a logging-enabled bucket, delivered to S3 and pulled by the Splunk Add-on for AWS's generic S3 input. Space-delimited; any field can read a dash when unknown, unavailable or not applicable.
aws:s3:accesslogs.note: Sample: the awsdocs S3 user guide's five-record worked example (four bucket-level GETs and one object PUT). Source: Amazon S3 User Guide, 'Amazon S3 server access log format', https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/LogFormat.html.

aws:cloudfront:accesslogs.description: CloudFront standard (access) logs: one line per viewer request, delivered to S3 and pulled by the Splunk Add-on for AWS's generic S3 input. Tab-delimited, W3C extended log format, with a #Fields header line the TA strips.
aws:cloudfront:accesslogs.note: No vendor-published worked sample was found for this sourcetype. Every binding below and every example in the sidecar is read from one genuine event already indexed (Splunk Security Content attack_data, T1485/decommissioned_buckets), not from a vendor page.

aws:transitgateway:flowlogs.description: Transit Gateway flow logs, default (all-fields) format: one line per recorded network flow, delivered to S3 and pulled by the Splunk Add-on for AWS's generic S3 input. Space-delimited, 36 fields in the default format.
aws:transitgateway:flowlogs.note: No sample exists for this sourcetype and none is indexed (0 events). An exhaustive search found none: AWS publishes the field table but never a worked example record for this sourcetype, and every candidate record found elsewhere was either the wrong (custom) field count or not an AWS/Splunk-published source. Every concept and binding below comes from that field table alone.

bindings.note: Field 5 of the record (target:port_list), captured whole by this TA's regex; confirmed against a real indexed event.
bindings.basis_ref: the dev index, read 2026-09-19: TargetPort and target both read 10.0.0.1:80 (or - together) on the same events; dest_port never populates a value there.

bindings.note: The method token of the Request line, split out by the TA.
Same shape as bucket_owner (canonical user id, assumed-role ARN, or dash); bound to the same concept because it is the same kind of value, not the same party.
This sourcetype's TIME_PREFIX/TIME_FORMAT field (entry.json time_field), format [%d/%b/%Y:%H:%M:%S %z].
The method token of the Request-URI line, split out by the TA.
What the viewer actually put in its Host header; can differ from cs_host when the distribution uses an alternate domain name (CNAME).
The result after the last byte left the server.
The result just before the response was returned to the viewer; see the cloudfront_two_result_fields hazard.
TA CIM-style alias; despite the name this is the cache/edge classification code (Hit, Miss, Error, ...), not a boolean.
This sourcetype's time field is built from date and time together.

best_effort_delivery.text: ELB and CloudFront both log on a best-effort basis: a request can be missing from access logs entirely, and delivery can lag well behind the request itself. Read these logs as a picture of traffic shape, not a complete accounting of every request.

canonical_id_not_account_id.text: S3's bucket owner and requester fields carry the canonical user ID (a 64-character hex string, another form of the AWS account ID) or, for an assumed role, the role ARN. Neither is the 12-digit AWS account number; do not compare one to the other.

elb_two_timestamps.text: ELB logs two ISO 8601 timestamps: request_creation_time (when the load balancer received the request) and the record's own time field (when it finished responding, or a WebSocket closed). The gap between them covers the whole request, not one processing stage.

tgw_aggregation_lag.text: No genuine sample of this sourcetype was found or is indexed in the dev Splunk; every field here is read from AWS's field table alone, never from a real record. The start and end fields are Unix seconds for an aggregation interval, and AWS's own doc says a record can appear up to 60 seconds after the packet was actually seen.

cloudfront_two_result_fields.text: CloudFront logs the edge cache result twice: once after the last byte left the server (x-edge-result-type) and once just before the response was returned to the viewer (x-edge-response-result-type). They usually match; they differ when the viewer disconnects mid-response.

cloudfront_split_time.text: CloudFront's date and time are two separate columns (UTC calendar date, UTC clock time); both are needed to reconstruct one timestamp, and for a WebSocket connection both mark when the connection closed, not when it opened.
